regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like the headline; PMI Composite at 56.5 and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY confirm the expansion is real and broad-based. But core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, and the FY estimate has been revised down to 7.1% YoY — the back half of the year is already being discounted. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is approaching the threshold where private capex becomes self-sustaining; the question is whether the credit channel stays open long enough to fund it.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 6.09% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 10-year high at the 95th percentile — is doing the RBI's tightening work for it, but the wrong way: it compresses household budgets rather than anchoring expectations. Core CPI at 4.5% YoY is rising for the second consecutive month, which means the food-and-fuel spike is no longer the whole story. The RBI's own inflation forecast sits at 5.1% YoY; with headline CPI already at 6.09% YoY and WPI at 9.92% YoY, that forecast is a liability, not a guide.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.54% YoY; CD ratio 82%","signal_text":"Credit growth at 19.54% YoY against deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for three consecutive months — has pushed the CD ratio to 82%, the 75th percentile of its 10-year range. Services credit at 28.3% YoY (83rd percentile) and agriculture at 19.5% YoY (82nd percentile) are the engines; housing credit decelerating to 10.6% YoY for three straight months is the tell that affordability stress is already biting. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% while deposit growth lagged, the regulator moved on risk weights within two quarters — the incentive to act is identical today.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is being eroded in real time: CPI at 6.09% YoY puts the ex-post real rate negative. The RBI's 'data-dependent pause' is increasingly a euphemism for being caught between a growth mandate it cannot abandon and an inflation overshoot it cannot ignore. For corporate capex IRRs, the relevant rate is not the repo but the 10-year G-sec, which is being pulled in two directions — domestic inflation pushing it up, global carry dynamics pulling it down.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY, up from 16.1%, with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — the 68th percentile and rising from 75.6% — is the most credible signal that the investment cycle is underway, not just budgeted. Iron ore at $161.91/t, nearly double its prior print of $90.64/t, confirms infrastructure demand is physical, not statistical. The inversion: services credit at 28.3% YoY is growing faster than industry credit at 19.5% YoY, which means the capex story is partly being funded by working capital dressed as investment.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹231290 cr/mo; PV 32.1% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month — the 90th percentile — is the strongest single-month print in this cycle, but the prior month was ₹1,88,125 cr / month; a jump of that magnitude in one month demands decomposition before celebration. Passenger vehicle sales at 32.1% YoY and two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY confirm the demand surge is not confined to the formal economy. The divergence to watch: e-commerce GMV growth at 25% YoY (43rd percentile) is mid-table despite the consumption surge, suggesting the volume is in physical durables and vehicles, not digital discretionary.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.54% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for three consecutive months (13.8%→17.1%→19.4%→19.54% credit; 10.8%→17.8%→16.86% deposits). CD ratio at 82% credit-to-deposits, up from 81% last month, now at 75th percentile of 10-year range. Services credit surging 28.3% YoY (83rd percentile), agriculture at 19.5% YoY (82nd percentile), while housing credit decelerating to 10.6% YoY (falling three months straight). NBFC credit growth at 15.4% YoY, down from 15.8%, signalling funding stress.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% and retail deposit franchises — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will spike. Watch for RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rate ceilings, CRR cuts) within 6-8 weeks. Tactical short on mid-cap NBFCs with <₹500 cr / month deposit inflows.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded either RBI rate cuts (to ease deposit pressure) or NBFC stress cycles. Last time CD hit 82%+ was Q3 2022, which led to 6-month NBFC underperformance.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Across Sectors","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest), up from 16.1% YoY, with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (68th percentile, up from 75.6%). Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5% but still mid-cycle). Credit to industry at 19.5% YoY (76th percentile, up from 7.7% YoY), services credit at 28.3% YoY (83rd percentile, rising three months: 21.4%→22.9%→24.3%→28.3%), and agriculture credit at 19.5% YoY (82nd percentile, rising three months: 16.8%→17%→17.2%→19.5%). Iron ore prices at $161.91/t, up from $90.64/t, signalling infrastructure demand.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Escorts, Bharat Heavy Electricals) and cement (Ultratech, Ambuja) — order books will expand 8-12 weeks out. Increase exposure to project-linked equities (L&T, Kalpataru) and PSU capex plays (NTPC, Power Grid). Reduce defensives; rotation into cyclicals justified. Hedge with long-dated call spreads on Nifty 50 to capture upside without tail risk.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-cycle; historically, capex accelerates when CU crosses 78-80%. Last sustained capex upcycle (2014-2018) saw IIP capgoods average 12-15% YoY; current 16.9% suggests front-loading ahead of potential policy tightening.","is_surprise":false}

However, SIP YoY growth at 8.9% YoY (28th percentile, decelerating from 15%→19.85%→14%→10.7%→8.9%), and SIP accounts at 10 mn (3rd percentile, data anomaly suggests reporting issue).","implication":"Retail equity flows remain structural bid under ₹32,000-33,000 cr / month. Headline CPI at 6.09% YoY (57th percentile, rising three months: 3.21%→4.45%→5.54%→6.09%), core CPI at 4.5% YoY (42nd percentile, rising two months: 3.4%→3.9%→4.5%). Food inflation at 8.94% YoY (62nd percentile, rising three months: 3.47%→5.52%→7.74%→8.94%). WPI at 9.92% YoY (70th percentile). signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down from 14.1→15.08→14.1→15.08→19.5 mn sq ft / quarter over prior five quarters — a 79% collapse in a single quarter. Office vacancy at 13.4% vacant (37th percentile, down from 14.5%), suggesting supply-side tightness despite absorption collapse. Nifty IT index flat YoY while office absorption craters. Rent in Bengaluru at ₹103.6/sqft/mo (61st percentile, down from ₹168.8/sqft/mo), Mumbai rent at ₹156/sqft/mo (60th percentile, down from ₹343/sqft/mo). Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% vacant (37th percentile). Contrast: airline passenger traffic at 8.64 mn / month (0th percentile, data anomaly from 86.4 mn / month), suggesting high-frequency mobility is intact.","implication":"The office absorption collapse is NOT a sign of IT services weakness — it's a structural shift from traditional IT services to Global Capability Centers (GCCs) operated by multinational corporates. GCCs lease smaller, premium office spaces (not bulk IT parks) and are concentrated in Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Pune. Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are consolidating real estate, while GCCs are the marginal buyer. This means: (1) Avoid commercial real estate plays betting on IT services recovery (Embassy Office Parks, Mindspace REIT down 12-30% YoY); (2) Overweight IT services on earnings, not real estate proxies — the sector is NOT in structural decline; (3) Watch for GCC-focused office REITs or co-working platforms (WeWork India, Awfis) as the real play. Falsifiable: if Nifty IT rebounds 15%+ while office absorption stays <5 mn sq ft / quarter, the GCC thesis is confirmed.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile is a 10-year low, but this is a data inflection, not a crisis. The last time office absorption spiked (19.5 mn sq ft / quarter) was Q4 2024, driven by traditional IT services. Current collapse suggests a structural reallocation of real estate demand from IT parks to premium GCC spaces — a positive for IT services earnings but negative for bulk office REITs.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

GST Record Flatters — Decompose Before Celebrating

The facts:

  • GST collections hit ₹2,31,290 cr / month (90th percentile), up from ₹1,88,125 cr / month — the largest single-month jump in this cycle.
  • PMI Composite at 56.5 and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY confirm expansion is broad, not sector-specific.
  • But core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, and the full-year GDP estimate was revised down to 7.1% YoY from 7.6% YoY.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) is compressing household budgets even as headline consumption data looks strong.

The tension: The GST print and vehicle sales signal a demand surge; the core sector deceleration and downward FY estimate revision signal the back half of the year is already being marked down. Both cannot be right simultaneously.

Bottom line: Watch whether November GST sustains above ₹2,10,000 cr / month — a reversion below that level would confirm the October print was a timing distortion, not a demand step-change.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

BOJ Tightening Meets Falling US Yields — Carry Unwind Loading

The facts:

  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile), rising for the second consecutive month — the highest in this data series.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 4.91% yield (89th percentile), falling for five consecutive months from 5.15% yield.
  • US GDP SAAR at 4.3% SAAR with PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) — US growth is re-accelerating even as the Fed holds at 3.88% p.a.
  • But Eurozone GDP at 0.4% YoY and China PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) mean the global growth story is a US-only phenomenon.

The tension: BOJ normalisation compresses the yen carry trade's return at the same moment US yields are falling — the two forces together accelerate carry unwind, and EM liquidity is the first casualty.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the underpriced tail risk for India FII flows; watch for the next BOJ meeting as the trigger, not the Fed.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds — But Institutional Conviction Is Thinning

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (94th percentile), marginally down from ₹32,490 cr / month but up three of the last four months.
  • But SIP YoY growth has decelerated to 8.9% YoY (28th percentile), down from 19.85% YoY six months ago — the flow level is high, the growth rate is not.
  • DII equity net flows collapsed to ₹6,222 cr / month from ₹51,829 cr / month the prior month — a single-month drop of ₹45,607 cr / month.
  • FII equity net at -₹4,516 cr / month remains negative, with the prior month showing -₹49,935 cr / month — the worst outflow in recent history.

The tension: Retail SIP inflows are structurally anchored at the 94th percentile; institutional flows — both FII and DII — are volatile and currently negative. The market is being held up by systematic retail, not conviction buying.

Bottom line: If DII net flows do not recover above ₹20,000 cr / month in December, the SIP floor will be tested against a market with no institutional bid beneath it.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

REITs Price Office Collapse; Residential Splits by City and Ticket

The facts:

  • NRI buying is FALLING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (prior 15%, but down 2 pp vs earlier print); NRI share within premium/luxury at 32%, concentrated in Mumbai MMR, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad.
  • Premium ₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr is the only ticket band where launch supply (31%) matches sales demand (31%); Hyderabad leads with sales +15% YoY and launches +120% YoY, while Chennai (-10% YoY) and Pune (-6% YoY) are contracting.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter — down 79% from 19.5 mn sq ft / quarter — has driven Embassy REIT to ₹370/unit, Mindspace to ₹345/unit, Brookfield to ₹263/unit, all down 12–31% from prior prints.
  • But office vacancy fell to 13.4% vacant from 14.5% vacant despite the absorption collapse — GCCs at 42% of occupier mix are consolidating existing space, not vacating it.

The tension: REIT unit prices are pricing an office demand collapse; vacancy data says supply is tightening. The market is confusing a GCC consolidation quarter with a structural demand reversal.

Bottom line: REITs are a buy if Q4 office absorption recovers above 10 mn sq ft / quarter — at current unit prices, the vacancy signal is being ignored and the discount is excessive.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Inflation, Carry, and Credit

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with CPI headline at 6.09% YoY — if Brent crosses $95/bbl, the RBI's pause becomes untenable and a rate hike re-enters the probability distribution.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — each 25 bps BOJ hike historically triggers $10–15 bn of EM carry unwind; India's FII equity net was already -₹49,935 cr / month one month ago.
  • CD ratio at 82% (75th percentile) with credit growing at 19.54% YoY vs deposits at 16.86% YoY — NBFC credit growth already decelerating to 15.4% YoY signals funding stress is transmitting.

The tension: All three risks share a common detonator: any external shock that forces RBI to abandon its pause would simultaneously tighten domestic liquidity, compress NBFC funding, and trigger FII outflows — a sequence the CD ratio leaves no buffer to absorb.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a sustained print above $95/bbl forces the RBI's hand and triggers the full risk cascade simultaneously.

"}
